statement: The study evaluates whether structurally valid but non-authoritative multi-turn history can redirect tool-use decisions when the current request, available tools, and gold next action are unchanged, and tests reliable-state policy transfer as a mitigation.
The authors name the observed failure mode history-induced policy hijacking: misleading historical traces redirect decisions that the model can execute correctly under reliable history.

ContextPollute-Bench represents each decision point with synchronized Original, Polluted, and Oracle State views that share the system policy, current tools, latest request, and gold next action; only the historical context differs.

A Call-required prediction is counted correct only when it invokes the gold tool with the complete gold argument object; Answer-required predictions cover clarification of missing information, answering from verified evidence, or recognizing unsupported requests.
ContextPollute-Bench is constructed from the airline and retail domains of APIGen-MT.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash generates the inserted pollution trace and Oracle State during benchmark construction, but does not generate the source gold calls or answers.

The benchmark uses eleven gold-preserving interventions grouped into Decision-State, Entity-Binding, and Interface-Execution interference, including unsupported completion claims, irrelevant reads, decommissioned tools, competing entities, and wrong, missing, extra, obsolete, reformatted, or unit-shifted arguments.
Deterministic validators preserve source-message order, keep the latest request final, pair tool calls with results, instantiate the intended distractor, and verify that the gold action is unchanged.
Oracle States are rejected if they expose the gold tool or omit decision-critical state.
All examples derived from the same source trajectory are kept in the same split to prevent overlap across train, validation, and test sets.
OOD-600 contains 600 Call-required examples whose gold actions invoke six tools that are never observed as gold tools during training.
Tool Call Recall (TCR) is the probability of predicting CALL with the exact gold function and complete gold argument object conditional on a gold CALL decision.
Over-Call Rate (OCR) is the probability of predicting CALL conditional on a gold ANSWER decision.
Balanced Tool-Use Accuracy (BTA) is defined as one half TCR plus one half of one minus OCR.

The evaluation also reports Decision Accuracy, Tool Accuracy on gold Call examples, and Argument Exact Match conditional on correct tool selection; under this decomposition TCR equals Tool Accuracy multiplied by Argument Exact Match.
Train contains 9,901 examples: 5,828 Call and 4,073 Answer examples, with 14 gold tools.
Validation contains 1,121 examples: 846 Call and 275 Answer examples, with 13 gold tools.
Test-Indist contains 2,375 examples: 1,651 Call and 724 Answer examples, with 13 gold tools.
OOD-600 contains 600 examples: 600 Call and 0 Answer examples, with 6 held out gold tools.
Oracle-OPD conditions a frozen teacher on synchronized Oracle State so that supervision reflects authoritative task evidence rather than competing historical traces.
Oracle-OPD uses token-level soft targets to transfer the teacher distribution over answering, calling, tool selection, and argument generation rather than only a single hard target sequence.
Oracle-OPD evaluates the teacher on prefixes generated by the current polluted-context student, providing supervision on student-visited states.
Oracle-OPD minimizes token-level reverse KL between the polluted-context student distribution and the Oracle-conditioned teacher distribution on the same student-generated prefixes.
Reverse KL is computed over the union of the teacher and student top-16 token supports at temperature 1, using four student rollouts per prompt and no additional gold cross-entropy objective.
At deployment, Oracle-OPD requires only the trained student and ordinary interaction history; the teacher and Oracle State are removed.
Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B are trained for three epochs with full-parameter FSDP on eight NVIDIA H20 GPUs.
OPD training uses learning rate 1e-6, global batch size 32 prompts, four rollouts per prompt, and prompt/response limits of 12,288/1,024 tokens.
SFT training uses a cosine learning-rate schedule with learning rate 1e-5 and global batch size 256.
Evaluation uses greedy decoding, and checkpoints are selected by validation BTA before test evaluation.

For cross-generator evaluation, checkpoint selection is fixed and inference is performed only on contexts independently regenerated by Claude-Opus-4.7; no Claude-generated example is used for training, adaptation, or model selection.

The benchmark-construction supplement provides five standalone stages plus an end-to-end run_pipeline.sh driver, producing train.jsonl, val.jsonl, test_indist.jsonl, and test_ood_600.jsonl.
The third-party apigen-mt_5k.json source file is obtained from the APIGen-MT release and is not redistributed with the submitted supplement.

Train, validation, and Test-Indist are assigned at the source-trajectory level using deterministic greedy target-proportion packing with 70%/10%/20% trajectory-level targets and deterministic tie-breaking.

The six held-out OOD gold functions are update_reservation_passengers, get_reservation_details, return_delivered_order_items, modify_pending_order_address, modify_pending_order_payment, and get_product_details.

For Answer-required examples, an independent zero-temperature preservation auditor sees only the Polluted conversation and current tool inventory; examples are retained only when it returns NO_CALL and reports no previously missing information as newly present.

Oracle State is generated once per unique decision point and contains current intent, known slots, verified observations, relevant policy, missing information, evidence status, and irrelevant history to drop; the prompt forbids function names, complete calls, or action directives.

Standalone structural validation requires valid OpenAI-format message fields, valid turn alternation and call-result chaining, an unchanged final latest request, a well-formed gold object, and the Original message sequence as an in-order subsequence of Polluted history.

Every final benchmark JSONL record is self-contained and includes a stable id, original_context, polluted_context, oracle_state_view, current_tools, latest request, gold_action, decision fields, pollution metadata, source_span, provenance, and oracle_meta.
The submitted benchmark audit defines four criteria: gold validity, Oracle non-leakage, Oracle sufficiency and faithfulness, and pollution naturalness.

The 1,000-example cross-audit is stratified across 650 Test-Indist, 150 OOD-600, 100 Train, and 100 Validation examples, spanning both decision types, all three non-call subtypes, and all eleven interference operators.
Thinking is disabled in the chat template, gradient checkpointing and padding removal are enabled, and evaluation uses greedy decoding with a 1,024-token response limit.

SFT-family runs use AdamW with warmup ratio 0.1, weight decay 0.01, and gradient clipping at 1.0; distributional-distillation runs use constant learning rate, no warmup, no weight decay, temperature 1, and no gold-CE term.

All distillation variants compute reverse KL over the union of teacher and student top-16 supports, use temperature 1, and set the gold-CE coefficient to zero; on-policy configurations draw four student continuations per prompt.
The 1.7B student is trained in fp32 and the 8B student in bf16, while reverse-KL reduction is computed in fp32 for both model sizes.
For SFT→DPO, the preference prompt is the Polluted input, the preferred continuation is the gold continuation, and the alternative is a mined tool-use error; DPO uses beta 0.1.
The primary Test-Indist BTA comparison uses 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples, and HotpotQA Noisy-F1 comparisons use 2,000 question-level paired bootstrap resamples.

The training environment uses one node with eight NVIDIA H20 GPUs with 96 GB HBM per GPU, TencentOS Server 4 series, Linux 6.6 series, Python 3.11, full-parameter FSDP, verl 0.7.0, vLLM, TRL DPOTrainer, FlashAttention, and HuggingFace Transformers.
On eight H20 GPUs, the matched 1.7B Off-policy OD run required 13.7 aggregate GPU-hours.
On eight H20 GPUs, the matched 1.7B Oracle-OPD run required approximately 60 aggregate GPU-hours.

HotpotQA-Distractor evaluation uses all 7,405 validation examples zero-shot with fixed 1.7B checkpoints; Noisy inputs contain all ten supplied paragraphs, Clean inputs contain only complete paragraphs whose titles match annotated supporting facts, and outputs are scored with official exact match and token-level F1.

The 1.7B student distilled from an 8B teacher improved HotpotQA Noisy-F1 over the next-best trained checkpoint by 0.0297, with a 95% confidence interval from 0.0246 to 0.0348.
Relative to Gold-SFT, the 1.7B student distilled from an 8B teacher improved HotpotQA Noisy-F1 by 0.0835, with a 95% confidence interval from 0.0754 to 0.0913.

ContextPollute-Bench is limited to controlled next-action interventions over airline and retail trajectories; the authors state that naturally occurring production histories and end-to-end interaction would broaden coverage.
Oracle-OPD requires Oracle State and on-policy rollouts during training, although deployment requires only the distilled student and ordinary interaction history.
The authors conclude that robust tool use requires models to identify which historical state remains authoritative for the current request.

The authors conclude that ContextPollute-Bench reveals misleading traces can redirect policies that models otherwise execute correctly, and that Oracle-OPD produces the strongest balanced Qwen3-1.7B policy while transferring across clean histories, generators, operators, unseen functions, external tool-use benchmarks, and noisy multi-hop QA.
The authors characterize history reliability as a distinct and tractable training target for multi-turn tool-using agents.
